correctness.rationale: The exponent-gcd characterization is exact. Principal signatures \(p^{2j+1}m^2\) are uniquely represented and are automatically Achilles. Fixed-order Landau counting yields the principal main term, the prime/exponent weights are absolutely summable, a polylogarithmic truncation justifies uniform passage to the sum, and every nonprincipal Achilles signature has at least two exceptional exponents and therefore one fewer Landau logarithmic degree (or \(X^{1/3+o(1)}\) when \(r=2\)). The finite verifier independently reproduces published counts but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies the first non-perfect-power layer inside a classical thin multiplicative set. At fixed omega, powerful numbers are dominated by perfect squares; the theorem quantifies the next layer after those are deleted, gives an explicit universal prime-series constant, and covers every fixed number of distinct prime factors rather than a single arbitrary finite slice. This directly refines the structure behind the Achilles sequence and complements global h-full omega-distribution results.
